ask.text: The request suggests hiding the big noise folders in the new file explorer by default, but that was never confirmed. When you open a project folder like this one (it has node_modules), what should the explorer show?
ask.why: It decides what the first-built piece shows and hides, how it performs on large projects, and whether you can still reach those folders. The request marked this default as not settled.

options.label: Hide node_modules, .git, target and dist, with a 'show hidden' way to reach them
options.consequence: The tree stays fast and tidy on big projects, and you can still reveal those folders when you actually need them.

options.label: Hide node_modules, target and dist but keep .git visible
options.consequence: A little more clutter, but the git folder stays one click away without any reveal step.

options.label: Show every file and folder, hide nothing
options.consequence: Nothing is ever out of reach, but projects with node_modules become slow and noisy to browse.

coverage.note: Single-user Windows desktop app; there are no roles, accounts or sharing to model.

Nothing is remembered across a restart: the root is re-derived from the current view/active tab and expanded folders start collapsed; a folder chosen via 'Open folder...' stays the root only until the view or active tab changes.

Browse up to OS permissions; root = selected app's root in the app view, the active tab's owning app root in the editor, a misc file's parent folder with up climbing to the drive list, or the home folder when no app/tab path applies.
Exact refusal behaviour and wording for name clashes, moving a folder into itself, unreadable folders, and a Recycle Bin that cannot take the item are proposed but unconfirmed.
Empty, loading and error states for the explorer, and the in-progress, failed and no-op states of F5, are not decided.
Clicking an already-open file focuses its existing tab instead of opening a duplicate (request item 1); single-user app, so no two people edit at once.
Which heavy/noisy folders are hidden by default; asking this now.
Delete asks for confirmation and sends the item to the Recycle Bin (recoverable), never a permanent delete.
No path restriction beyond OS permissions; dot/hidden files are shown unless the chosen hide list excludes them, so the developer's own files stay reachable.

One directory level loads at a time (no full-disk scan); every visible control has a text label and works by keyboard; a folder that cannot be read shows a locked/message state instead of blocking the app.

assumptions: Data: nothing is remembered across a restart; the root is re-derived from the current view/active tab and expanded folders start collapsed; a folder chosen from 'Open folder...' stays the root only until the view or active tab changes.
Privacy: dot/hidden files are shown unless the chosen hide list excludes them; no extra path restrictions beyond OS permissions.
Quality: one directory level loads at a time (no full scan); visible controls are labelled and keyboard-operable; an unreadable folder shows a message instead of blocking the app.
